prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: playable level-map concept for Snabbit, a 2011 top-down scrolling snake game.
Primary request: invent one BEAUTIFUL level named "The Hollow Orchard". Show the complete narrow vertical level map, 16 staggered hex-grid columns wide and about 90 rows tall. Player starts bottom center and only travels upward, diagonally left or right. Five chunky mechanical levers are encountered in order; each opens the next nearby stone arch. Walls form unequal organic pockets, curved little rooms, hooked arches and crescent crags. Compose an expressive upward route with several calm broad chambers and short narrower entrances; the route bends asymmetrically, never a regular left-right zigzag. Many walls, but compelling open negative-space shapes.
Input images: Image 1 is a sprite/style reference only: use its rounded faceted white metal boulders, dark grey rock, cyan gems, yellow stars, white diamond, and especially the chunky grey lever with orange/green knob.
Style/medium: crisp polished 2D game level editor map using those faceted sprites; navy star-space background; clean enough to recreate faithfully on the actual hex grid. Stone walls remain hand-shaped, welcoming and visually charming.
Composition/framing: one tall vertical map filling the image, shown orthographically from directly overhead. Five distinct small cave courtyards grow out of an irregular continuous rocky landform; route begins near bottom center, drifts into a lower-right hollow, curls left through a middle moon-shaped room, then right around a central stone island, then gently left through an upper arch into a starry summit garden. Do not draw generic maze corridors. Leave generous open pockets around switches. Place five obvious levers, three widely spaced yellow stars and 12-20 cyan gems grouped in short pleasing clusters rather than one gem on every route cell. A tiny white diamond rewards a small late detour. The finish is a short checkered band at the very top.
Constraints: A map of actual discrete sprites, no painted scenery, no floor tiles. Walls must look organic rather than systematic. Five closed arch openings may use darker ghost rocks. Route must always climb upward without going back down. Use a delicate dotted cyan guide only where helpful, not a solid long snake. No text except small title "The Hollow Orchard"; no UI chrome, no legend, no coordinate labels.
Avoid: repeated full-width horizontal wall strips, repeated zigzags, rectangular rooms, regular rail corridors, perfectly symmetric decoration, identical repeated chambers, busy gem noise, isometric perspective, 3D scenery.
